method: fresh shallow clone of the pinned commit; classify first (protocol/tool schema, session semantics, extraction, orchestration, retry, pagination, cost, failure, provenance, or plumbing), then compare with ECDEV

coverage.not_read: tests/*.spec.ts, config.d.ts; the implementation is in the Playwright monorepo and was not fetched
coverage.statement: Bounded semantic review of the files named, not the whole source. No extinction is claimed.

rows.behaviour: Source is not in this repository: it is a launcher over playwright-core. What is readable is the tool surface: accessibility-tree snapshot (browser_snapshot) as the action basis, navigate, click, type, fill_form, wait_for, tabs, network request list plus per-request detail, console messages, cookies and local storage get/set/clear, route mocking, and an unsafe code evaluator.
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV has no browser. Pages are fetched as bytes under robots with visible-text and main-content fingerprints.
rows.knowledge: Protocol and tool schema of a browser-automation server; the behaviour sits in the Playwright monorepo (donor microsoft--playwright, still UNREVIEWED). Nothing in this repository to learn that the tool list does not already say.
rows.evidence: README tool list; src/README.md points to the monorepo

rows.behaviour: The server exists because some pages only show content after script execution. Whether that matters for ECDEV depends on how many product pages carry no price in their static HTML.
rows.ecdev_today: Static fetch only, with extraction failures recorded as unknowns rather than guessed.
rows.knowledge: How many live product pages publish a price only after script execution? ECDEV can answer part of it without a browser: the share of fetched product pages with no extractable price and no JSON-LD/microdata offer, then a headless render on that subset to see how many gain one. Not run: it needs a browser and a labelled page sample.
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answerable: static-versus-rendered price recovery on a live sample; not run
